paper_title: A Narrow-Bandgap n-Type Polymer Semiconductor Enabling Efficient All-Polymer Solar Cells
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Advanced Materials - 2019 - Shi - A Narrow‐Bandgap n‐Type Polymer Semiconductor Enabling Efficient All‐Polymer Solar Cells/auto/Advanced Materials - 2019 - Shi - A Narrow‐Bandgap n‐Type Polymer Semiconductor Enabling Efficient All‐Polymer Solar Cells.md

knowledge_points.content: DCNBT-IDT is synthesized by copolymerizing the electron-deficient building block 5,6-dicyano-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole (DCNBT) with indacenodithiophene (IDT) via a Stille coupling-based polycondensation reaction.
knowledge_points.evidence: The dibrominated monomers DCNBT and NDI were copolymerized with the distannylated indacenodithiophene comonomer IDT via a Stille couplingbased polycondensation reaction under microwave irradiation to afford two new polymers DCNBT-IDT and NDI-IDT, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: All-polymer solar cells based on the PBDB-T:DCNBT-IDT blend achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 8.32%, a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 14.20 mA/cm², and an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.90 V.
knowledge_points.evidence: the DCNBT-IDTbased all-PsCs yielded an excellent photovoltaic performance with an optimal PCE of up to 8.32% along with a high opencircuit voltage (Voc) of 0.90 eV... Jsc of 14.20 mA cm−2.

knowledge_points.content: DCNBT-IDT exhibits a narrow optical bandgap of 1.43 eV and a high absorption coefficient of 6.15 x 10^4 cm⁻¹, which is significantly higher than that of the benchmark N2200 (3.48 x 10^4 cm⁻¹).
knowledge_points.evidence: Compared to the benchmark poly(naphthalene diimide-alt-bithiophene) (N2200), DCNBT-IDT shows a narrower bandgap (1.43 eV) with a much higher absorption coefficient (6.75 × 10^4 cm−1).

knowledge_points.content: The DCNBT unit reduces steric hindrance compared to naphthalene diimide (NDI) units, resulting in a more planar polymer backbone with a calculated dihedral angle of 23.2° between DCNBT and IDT, compared to 35.5° in NDI-IDT.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure 2d,e reveals that there is a dihedral angle of 23.2° between DCNBT and IDT in polymer DCNBT-IDT. However, a much higher degree of backbone torsion with a calculated dihedral angle of about 35.5° was found between NDI and IDT in polymer NDI-IDT

knowledge_points.content: The energy loss (Eloss) in PBDB-T:DCNBT-IDT solar cells is approximately 0.53 eV, which is among the lowest values reported for all-PSCs with efficiencies exceeding 8%.
knowledge_points.evidence: More importantly, the energy loss (Eloss) in the DCNBT-IDT cell is only 0.53 eV, which is among the smallest values reported to date for all-PSCs with efficiency > 8%

knowledge_points.content: Optimal device performance for PBDB-T:DCNBT-IDT blends was achieved using chlorobenzene (CB) as the processing solvent with 1% volume ratio of 1,8-diiodooctane (DIO) as an additive and subsequent thermal annealing.
knowledge_points.evidence: Through systematic device optimizations... it was found that a polymer donor:polymer acceptor ratio of 1:1 (wt:wt) and using CB as the processing solvent... By employing 1% volume ratio of 1,8-diiodooctane (DIO) as the processing additive and thermal annealing treatment could further boost the device performance.

knowledge_points.content: GIWAXS analysis shows that DCNBT-IDT and its blend with PBDB-T exhibit a preferential face-on orientation, with a π-π stacking peak located at qz ≈ 1.48 Å⁻¹ in the out-of-plane direction.
knowledge_points.evidence: Based on the 2D GIwAXs images of the pure DCNBT-IDT and NDIIDT polymers (Figure 5a,b), both polymers exhibit preferential face-on orientation... evidenced from the more obvious π-π stacking peak (located at around qz ≈ 1.48 Å−1 in the OOP directions.

knowledge_points.content: The electron mobility (µe) of the PBDB-T:DCNBT-IDT blend film, measured by the SCLC method, is 5.02 x 10⁻⁵ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹, which is more than three times higher than that of the NDI-IDT-based blend.
knowledge_points.evidence: However, the electron mobility (μe,SCLC) of the PBDB-T:DCNBTIDT blend film is 5.02 × 10−5 cm2 V−1 s−1 which is over three times higher than that of the PBDB-T:NDI-IDT film (1.64 × 10−5 cm2 V−1 s−1).

knowledge_points.content: DCNBT-IDT and NDI-IDT polymers exhibit high thermal stability with 5% weight loss temperatures (Td) of 426 °C and 442 °C, respectively, as determined by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA).
knowledge_points.evidence: both DCNBT-IDT and NDI-IDT exhibited good thermal stability as evidenced by the high decomposition temperatures (the temperature with a 5% weight loss) of 426 and 442 °C, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: Photoluminescence (PL) quenching measurements indicate an 85% quenching efficiency for the PBDB-T:DCNBT-IDT blend film, suggesting efficient exciton dissociation at the donor-acceptor interface.
knowledge_points.evidence: The greater PL quenching efficiency of 85% for the PBDBT:DCNBT-IDT film (vs the 75% quenching efficiency for the PBDB-T:NDI-IDT film) is in good agreement with its high Jsc in solar cell devices

knowledge_points.content: Light intensity-dependent Voc measurements yielded a slope of 1.16 kT/q for DCNBT-IDT devices, indicating that bimolecular recombination is the dominant recombination mechanism.
knowledge_points.evidence: The slope factors for the DCNBTIDT- and NDI-IDT-based solar cells are determined to be 1.16 and 1.24 kB T/q (Figure 3e), respectively. The smaller slope factor of the DCNBT-IDT-based all-PSCs indicates that bimolecular recombination is the dominant recombination pathway

knowledge_points.content: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations indicate that DCNBT-IDT possesses more delocalized HOMO and LUMO distributions along the polymer backbone compared to NDI-IDT, facilitating better intrachain electron transport.
knowledge_points.evidence: Additionally, on the basis of the calculated orbital spatial distributions (Figure S7, Supporting Information), DCNBT-IDT shows a more delocalized HOMO and LUmO along polymer backbone, which should be beneficial to intrachain electron transport.
